intro: To search emails by sender in Apple Mail on Mac, click the search field, type from: and the sender's name, then choose the suggestion below it. Mail turns that into a filter, so only messages from that sender appear in the mailbox you have open.
tldr: Click the search field in Mail's toolbar, then type from: and the sender's name.
Choose the suggestion below the field. Mail turns it into a filter you can change.
Click the down arrow on a filter to switch between messages to or from a person.
No results? Click Search all mailboxes. Remove a filter if you stacked several.
Apple's Mac search guide lists no keyboard shortcut for sender search, so these steps use the mouse and typing.

blocks.text: Why a sender search beats a plain keyword search

A plain word in Mail's search field can match almost anything. It might sit in the subject, the body, or a signature. That helps when you remember a phrase. It slows you down when you only remember who wrote.

The from: token tells Mail to look at the sender. You get messages from one person, not every message that mentions their name. In a busy inbox, that gap matters. The list shrinks before you read a single subject line.

Email time is a real cost. Slack commissioned a 2023 survey of 8,000 respondents, run by OnePoll, and filtering irrelevant emails topped its menial task list at 51%. Slack commissioned that survey, so weigh it as vendor research about work in general, not about search.

A 2019 SlickText survey of over 1,000 U.S. employees found 60.8% ignore at least some emails in their inbox. Neither survey measured sender search. They do show why people want faster ways to find the mail that matters.
What to type after from:

Apple's example uses a full name, as in from: Ashley Rico. Start with the name you remember, then pick the suggestion that matches the right person. Mail offers suggestions under the field as you type.

A 2022-era Apple Community thread includes replies that suggest typing a domain after from:. Apple's pages show names only. Test a domain on a sender you know before you rely on it. If two people share a first name, type the full name.
Use the filter and its down arrow
The suggestion becomes a search filter. You can see the filter in the search field, and you can stack more filters beside it. Each filter adds a condition that messages must meet.
Click the down arrow on a filter when you need the other direction. Apple says you can change the filter to search messages to or from a specific person. This matters when a thread runs both ways.

Worked example: Ashley sent you a quote last week, and you want the reply you sent back. Switch the filter so it covers messages to or from Ashley. Then scan the thread in one list instead of running a second search.
Search all mailboxes when the current one comes up empty
Mail searches the mailbox you have open. If nothing matches, Apple's Mac guide says to click Search all mailboxes below the search field. That widens the search to your other mailboxes.
Apple's iCloud.com guide makes the same point for the web app. A search covers only the mailbox or folder you picked first. Choose the folder before you type, or old threads may seem missing.
Here is a common case. You search from: Ashley Rico in Inbox and get zero results. The message may sit in an Archive folder. Click Search all mailboxes, and Mail checks the rest of your mailboxes.
Why extra filters make results disappear
Mail returns only messages that match every filter you added. Two filters work like an AND, not an OR. A sender filter plus a subject filter gives you the overlap of both.

Apple's Mac guide makes this point directly. Removing a filter can bring back results that went missing. An Apple Community thread also lists Subject Contains and Attachment Name Contains as filter options.
Example: from: Ashley Rico plus a subject filter for estimate. If the quote you want says quote in the subject, it drops out. Remove the subject filter, and the list widens again.
Sort by sender when you don't need a search
Sometimes you want the list grouped by who wrote in, with no search at all. Choose View > Sort By > From, and the message list reorders by sender.
Sorting changes the order. It never removes messages. A filter does remove them, so use a filter when you want a narrower list, and use a sort when you want to scan one.
Sender contains: where the suggestion went
Some people look for a Sender contains suggestion and can't find it. Apple's iCloud.com guide shows that suggestion in the web app. Apple's Mac guide does not show it.

One Apple Community thread says Mac Mail stopped offering Sender contains around late 2022, possibly with Ventura. Community replies suggested typing from: instead. No Apple reply appears in that thread, so treat the cause as unconfirmed.
The practical answer is the same either way. Type from:, choose the suggestion, and you get a sender filter.
Common mistakes that look like a broken search

items: Typing a name without choosing the Mail suggestion. Apple's steps say the suggestion is what creates the filter.
Searching the wrong mailbox. The search starts with the mailbox you have open.
Leaving an old subject or attachment filter on. Every filter has to match.
Typing a nickname. Use the name the message shows in the sender line.
Trusting a shared first name. Two people can match, so check each result.
Expecting a sort to filter the list. Sorting only reorders the messages.

blocks.text: When results still look wrong: rebuild the mailbox
If search still misses a message you know is there, a mailbox may need a rebuild. Select the mailbox in the sidebar first, then choose Mailbox > Rebuild.

Read the warning before you click. For IMAP or Exchange accounts, a rebuild discards the messages and attachments stored on your Mac. Mail downloads them again from the server. The mailbox looks empty until the download finishes.

Apple's page covers IMAP and Exchange only. It does not say what happens with POP or On My Mac mailboxes, so back those up before you rebuild anything. A copy on another drive costs little compared with lost mail.
Spotlight and Envelope Index tips from third-party sites

Search threads often suggest reindexing Spotlight or deleting Envelope Index files. Apple's help pages mention neither fix. The sources for these tips are third-party blogs, and we have not verified them.

Deleting Envelope Index is risky. Its folder names differ between Mail releases, so a file you remove may not be the one you meant. Back up your mail data before you touch anything in your Library folder.
Versions and what to check on your Mac
Apple's most direct page for this task is the macOS 26 version, which matches Tahoe. That page does not state a version number in its text. Check yours before you follow every label to the letter.

blocks.title: Check your Mail version
blocks.text: Choose Mail > About Mail and compare the version with the Mail 16.0 path in Apple's page address. These steps come from Apple's written guides, and we did not run them on a live Mac, so match the labels to your own window.
If the sender is the real problem

Sometimes you don't want to find a sender's mail. You want their mail to stop arriving. That is a separate task. Read [how to block a sender in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/block-a-sender-in-apple-mail) for those steps.

If you added Gmail to Mail, check that account setup first. [How to add Gmail to Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/use-gmail-in-apple-mail-in-gmail) walks through it. Then come back here to test your sender search.
A quick checklist before you call it broken

items: Confirm the mailbox you are searching is the one that holds the message.
Choose the Mail suggestion so your text becomes a filter.
Remove filters you added earlier, starting with the newest.
Click Search all mailboxes if the current mailbox is empty.
Use the down arrow on the filter to switch between from and to.
Compare your Mail version in Mail > About Mail with Apple's page.
Rebuild only after you read the warning for your account type.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to search by sender in Apple Mail?
faq.answer: Apple's Mac search guide lists no keyboard shortcuts for search, and it does not describe one for sender search. Click the search field, type from:, and choose the suggestion with the mouse or trackpad.

faq.question: Why is there no Sender contains option in Mail on my Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's iCloud.com guide shows a Sender contains suggestion, but the Mac guide does not. One Apple Community thread reports it disappeared from Mac Mail around late 2022, and no Apple reply appears in that thread. Type from: and the name instead.

faq.question: Does searching by sender look through every mailbox?
faq.answer: Not by default. Mail searches the mailbox you have open first. If nothing matches, click Search all mailboxes below the search field.

faq.question: Can I search by a company domain instead of a person's name?
faq.answer: A community reply suggests typing from: followed by a domain. Apple's pages only show names, so test a domain on a sender you know before you rely on it.

faq.question: Will rebuilding a mailbox delete my email?
faq.answer: For IMAP and Exchange accounts, Apple says a rebuild discards the copies stored on your Mac and downloads them again from the server. Apple's page does not cover POP or On My Mac mailboxes, so back those up first.

faq.question: How do I see all emails from one sender without a search?
faq.answer: Choose View > Sort By > From. The list groups by sender, and no messages are hidden. Use a filter when you need a narrower list.

faq.question: Do these steps work on iCloud.com?
faq.answer: Mostly. Apple's iCloud guide says to select the mailbox first, click the search field, type the sender, and choose Sender contains. That guide does not describe Mac-only options like Search all mailboxes.

faq.question: Which macOS version are these steps for?
faq.answer: The closest match is Apple's macOS 26 page, which matches Tahoe and uses the Mail 16.0 path. The page does not state a version number in its text, so check Mail > About Mail on your Mac.

task: Search emails by sender in Apple Mail
appliesTo: Apple Mail on Mac, based on Apple's macOS 26 Tahoe help pages
requirements: A Mac running macOS 26 or later, with Apple Mail open
At least one email account added to Mail
The sender's name as it appears in your messages

steps.name: Pick the mailbox to search
steps.text: Click the mailbox in the Mail sidebar that holds the message, such as Inbox or an account folder. Mail's search starts from the mailbox you have open, so choose the right one first.

steps.name: Open the search field
steps.text: Find the search field in the Mail toolbar and click it. If the field is hidden, click the Search button in the toolbar to show it.

steps.name: Type from: and the sender's name
steps.text: Type from: followed by the person's name, as in from: Ashley Rico. Suggestions appear below the field as you type.
steps.tip: Use the name the message shows. Shared first names can match more than one person.

steps.name: Choose the suggestion
steps.text: Click the Mail suggestion below the field. Choosing it turns your text into a search filter, so the filter is what narrows the list.

steps.name: Read the results
steps.text: Only messages from that sender in the current mailbox appear. Check the sender line on each result before you reply, in case two people share a name.

steps.name: Switch the filter direction
steps.text: To find messages you sent to that person, click the down arrow on the filter. Change it so it searches messages to or from a specific person.

steps.name: Widen to all mailboxes
steps.text: If the current mailbox has no results, click Search all mailboxes below the search field. Mail then checks every mailbox, not just the one you had open.

steps.name: Remove a filter that hides results
steps.text: Mail returns only messages that match every filter. Remove the newest filter, check the list again, and repeat until the message you want appears.
steps.tip: Remove one filter at a time so you can see which one hid the message.

steps.name: Clear the search
steps.text: Click the Clear button in the search field to end the search and return to your normal message list.

steps.name: Sort by sender without searching
steps.text: If you want the whole list grouped by who wrote in, choose View > Sort By > From. Mail reorders the messages without hiding any.

troubleshooting.problem: Search shows nothing in the current mailbox
troubleshooting.fix: Click Search all mailboxes below the search field. If you added filters, remove the newest one first.

troubleshooting.problem: Results vanish after I add a second filter
troubleshooting.fix: Mail returns only messages that match every filter. Remove a filter to widen the list.

troubleshooting.problem: No Sender contains suggestion on my Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Type from: and the name instead. Apple's Mac guide does not list Sender contains, and one community thread reports it disappeared.

troubleshooting.problem: Messages still missing after a search
troubleshooting.fix: For IMAP or Exchange accounts, select the mailbox and choose Mailbox > Rebuild. Read the warning first, and back up POP or On My Mac mail.
Click the Search button in the toolbar to show the field.

troubleshooting.problem: Sorting by sender does not find one person
troubleshooting.fix: Sorting only reorders the list. Type from: and the name in the search field to filter.
